summary:
The Kbool4_on Project 
Focuses on developing a Python-based platform for analyzing flame behavior in microgravity environments. The system combines image processing, computer vision, data analysis, and scientific visualization techniques to monitor and characterize combustion phenomena under reduced-gravity conditions. Using tools such as OpenCV, NumPy, Pandas, and Matplotlib, the platform automatically detects flame contours and extracts key parameters including diameter, area, brightness, and shape. The collected data are processed into graphs and statistical reports, providing a more accurate and efficient alternative to manual analysis methods. By improving the understanding of combustion dynamics in microgravity, the project contributes to spacecraft fire safety, future space exploration missions, and the advancement of combustion technologies. Its modular architecture also enables future integration of machine learning and predictive modeling techniques, creating a foundation for advanced research on fire behavior and safety in space environments.

Reference

NASA. NASA Studies Fire in Microgravity. NASA Scientific Visualization Studio. Available at: https://svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/31394. Accessed: November 14, 2026.
details:
Project Description

Kbool4_on , is a Python-based platform designed to analyze flame behavior in microgravity environments using computer vision, image processing, and data analytics. The system processes images and videos of combustion experiments to automatically detect flame contours and extract key parameters such as diameter, area, brightness, and shape. These measurements are then analyzed and presented through graphs, statistics, and visual reports, enabling researchers to better understand combustion dynamics under reduced-gravity conditions.

The project addresses the challenge of studying fire behavior in space, where the absence of gravity significantly changes flame structure, heat transfer, and combustion efficiency. Traditional manual analysis methods are time-consuming and susceptible to measurement errors. By automating data extraction and analysis, our solution improves accuracy, efficiency, and reproducibility.

The intended impact of the project is to contribute to spacecraft fire safety, support future human space exploration missions, and advance scientific knowledge of combustion processes in microgravity. Understanding how flames behave in space can help engineers design safer spacecraft systems and develop innovative combustion technologies.

To develop the project, we used Python along with OpenCV for image processing and computer vision, NumPy for numerical computation, Pandas for data management, and Matplotlib for scientific visualization. The platform was developed on standard computer hardware and designed with a modular architecture that supports future integration of machine learning and predictive modeling techniques.

The creativity of the project lies in combining automated visual analysis with scientific data processing to create an accessible and scalable research tool for space-related combustion studies. Our team considered factors such as measurement accuracy, automation, usability, scientific relevance, scalability, and the potential for future enhancements, ensuring that the platform can evolve alongside emerging research needs in space science and fire safety.
